Learn moreDETAILSREVIEWSMOREDescriptionOLD-SCHOOL SURVIVAL HORROR Inspired by the mood and structure of System Shock 2, Alien Resurrection and Doom 3, DERELIKT leans into the dread of being under-equipped, out of your depth, and very far from help. SOMETHING HAS COME ALIVE Von Neuman Outpost is a remote research station built into a derelict asteroid in Saturn’s orbit. Now its halls are dark, its systems are failing, and the few survivors left inside aren't telling the same story. EXPLORE A FAILING STATION Explore the outpost’s secrets, its corridors, labs, maintenance shafts, and crew quarters. And venture deeper into stranger places inside the rock. Search for supplies, solve environmental puzzles, and unlock new routes through a station that grows more dangerous the deeper you go. TRUST NO ONE COMPLETELY Over a dozen NPCs remain aboard the station, each with their own problems, agendas, and versions of what happened. Some need help. Some know more than they should. Some may be useful, dangerous, doomed, or all three. MAKE EVERY SHOT COUNT Combat is tense and satisfying, with a wide arsenal of traditional and alien weapons at your disposal. But every shot has a cost. Ammo, health, and inventory space matter. You have enough firepower to survive, but not enough to feel safe. This is not a power fantasy corridor shooter. It is unnerving, strange, and hostile. A LOVE LETTER TO LATE 90s HORROR GAMES DERELIKT embraces early 3D horror: warped geometry, heavy atmosphere, and a sense of unease. With a faithful and beautiful recreation of PS1 aesthetics, including affine texture warping, dynamic subdivision, lovingly hand painted vertex color, and full motion CGI cutscenes.Show morePublished byHyperstrangeDeveloped byVisuwyg, HyperstrangePlay withXBOX Series X|SPCHandheldCapabilitiesSingle playerOptimized for Xbox Series X|SXbox achievementsXbox cloud savesXbox Play Anywhere XBOX consoles XBOX games XBOX Game Pass XBOX accessories XBOX News XBOX Support Feedback Community Standards Photosensitive Seizure Warning User Research at XBOX Microsoft account Microsoft Store Support Returns Orders tracking Store locations Rewards Games Designed for XBOX English (United States) Your Privacy Choices Opt-Out Icon Your Privacy Choices Consumer Health Privacy Sitemap Contact Microsoft Privacy & Cookies Manage cookies Terms of use Trademarks Third Party Notices Safety & eco About our ads

source.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: new update brings New Game Plus, upgraded PSSR support for PS5 Pro today
source.evidenceText: November 5, 2026November 6, 2026 Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: new update brings New Game Plus, upgraded PSSR support for PS5 Pro today 5 0 79 Like this Ubisoft outlines what upgraded PSSR brings to the PS5 Pro version of the game. Brittany Spurlin Writer/Editor, Ubisoft Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: The Most Requested Update, a free update bringing several player-requested and quality-of-life features to the game, is live today on PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro. The update has new content, a progression update, and more, including: New Game Plus 2 New Trophies Enhanced Progression Mode option New Power calculation Master Assassin Naoe outfit Upgraded PSSR optimizations Animus Hub synchronization update Play Video The new PSSR update is exclusive to PlayStation 5 Pro players, giving them an even higher visual quality as they embark on or continue their Viking adventures in England. We spoke to Priscilla Nguyen, Engineering Studio Manager, to learn more about this update and why it’s essential for PlayStation 5 Pro players. What can you tell us about the PSSR update for the PS5 Pro? Priscilla Nguyen: It was about integrating the upgraded PSSR into the game, to have better graphics when upscaling at a better framerate. The upgraded PSSR is more efficient than the original, and easier to implement in the game source code. The upgraded PSSR is an enhanced version, and slightly more efficient than the game’s current Temporal Upscaler. More importantly, it’s much crisper and more visually stable, giving you seamless and stunning environments to explore in England. Why bring these improvements to Assassin’s Creed Valhalla? PN: At Ubisoft, it is important to remain at the forefront of technological innovation to ensure players continue to benefit from the best possible gaming experience, and as the upgraded PSSR was already successfully integrated into our latest releases, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and Assassin’s Creed Shadows, we thought it would be great to have in Valhalla too. The Assassin’s Creed Valhalla update presented an excellent opportunity to integrate the upgraded PSSR, delivering a noticeably sharper and more visually refined image quality in 4K and smoothness with 60FPS. One of the aspects players appreciated most about Assassin’s Creed Valhalla was the beauty and visual variety of its open world, from the snowy mountains of Norway to the flourishing meadows, robust forests, and frigid highlands of England. Now, with the new PSSR optimizations, those graphics have been enhanced and preserved to meet today’s technical standards and continue to deliver a high-quality, smooth visual experience for our players. Assassin’s Creed Valhalla came out a few years before the PS5 Pro. Were there any challenges updating the visuals for PSSR? PN: We didn’t need to overhaul the game’s content or visual assets. Instead, we leveraged the upgraded PSSR within our engine and rendering pipeline to enhance 4K image quality and deliver our Quality mode at 60FPS on PS5 Pro. The interesting challenge was finding the right balance between image quality, performance, and integration within an existing game that was originally built years before the PS5 Pro existed. The upgraded PSSR proved to be a very efficient solution, allowing us to maximize the new hardware’s capabilities while delivering a noticeable visual uplift and stronger performance without requiring extensive changes to the game’s content, making it an effective way to modernize the experience for PS5 Pro players.
